title: Telemetry compatibility proxy for SDK/CLI/API ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our ingestion pipeline currently assumes a single canonical telemetry envelope shape. Multiple clients (JS SDK, Go SDK, CLI telemetry, and direct API consumers) are emitting slight variants of that shape (field name differences, optional fields moved, and different version header encodings). These small incompatibilities cause a measurable percentage of events to be rejected or mis-parsed downstream, which impacts console dashboards, billing accuracy, and alerting.

Goal: Build a lightweight compatibility proxy service and accompanying tooling that performs graceful normalization and version-aware transformation of incoming telemetry from SDKs, CLI, and direct API consumers. The proxy will: 1) accept multiple legacy and current versions, 2) perform schema translation to the canonical ingest envelope, 3) emit telemetry-validation metrics for mismatch rates, and 4) provide a way to opt-in strict validation for canaries.

Scope and constraints: This ticket focuses on the server-side compatibility proxy and rollout plan. SDK/CLI changes (client-side version headers and small emitter changes) will be tracked separately but coordinated. We must avoid large coupling to the current pipeline: the proxy should act as a thin pre-ingest layer and be horizontally scalable. We will favor deterministic, well-tested transforms over ad-hoc fixes.

Design summary:
- Ingress: HTTP/gRPC endpoints that accept current and historical content-types (application/json, application/vnd.redwood.telemetry+json;v=... ).
- Version detection: Prefer explicit top-level "telemetry_version" header or content-type param; fall back to field heuristics for older clients.
- Transformation rules: A rulebook living in a small versioned ruleset repo (YAML) mapping legacy field names and nested shapes to the canonical envelope. Rules can include simple renames, path moves, defaulting, and safe enum mapping.
- Validation: After transform, run JSON Schema validation against canonical schema. Validation failures are logged and increment a metric; a configurable sampling of failures includes the raw payload (PII scrubbed).
- Observability: Metrics emitted: transform_count, transform_latency_ms, validation_failure_rate, unknown_version_rate, raw_drop_count. Dashboards and alert thresholds are part of the rollout.
- Idempotency & durability: Proxy should not alter event IDs. For retries, incoming idempotency-key header is preserved.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype transform service in Go (net/http + small rules engine) and unit tests for each rule type (1 week).
2) Add integration harness that replays staged historical events and asserts final canonical shape (2 weeks).
3) Telemetry for the proxy itself: add metrics and logs to the Console observability namespace and wire to existing dashboards (3 days).
4) Canary rollout: start with internal ingestion only (team usage), then 10% production traffic for 48 hours, then progressive rollout.

Testing and rollout: We will create a test corpus of ~20k historical events from the last 6 months that exercise the different client variants. CI verifies transforms preserve critical fields (customer_id, request_id, timestamp) and do not widen schema types. Canary includes a strict-validator toggle: if enabled, transformed events failing validation are sent to a dead-letter queue instead of main pipeline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Incoming legacy variants are normalized with <1% failure in canary.
- Validation failure metric is integrated into console-2025.03 dashboards.
- No perceptible increase in end-to-end latency beyond 30ms p95 for the proxy layer.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Ruleset misses unusual legacy variants. Mitigation: conservative logging and small-sample raw captures for inspection, quick rule rollout path.
- Risk: Proxy becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: autoscaling + fallback bypass path for emergency (direct pass-through with best-effort logging).

Rollout artifacts and links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TELEMETRY/Compatibility+Proxy+Design (internal), initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821, replay harness: https://build.redwood.ai/artifacts/telemetry-replay/compat-proxy-corpus-2025-01, dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/compatibility-proxy

Next steps: finalize rulebook for v0, complete prototype tests, coordinate SDK/CLI owners for version header bump during canary week.
updates: 2025-01-29: Initial design completed; prototype work kicked off. Marco created skeleton Go service and posted initial PR for review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821).
2025-02-03: Added first 8 transform rules covering JS SDK v1, v2 name migrations and CLI payload shape. Unit tests added for rename and defaulting rules. Requested review from @Priya-S and @Jonah.

2025-02-06: Design review feedback: prefer explicit version header handling and tighten sampling for raw captures to 0.1% to reduce risk of PII leakage. Action: implement header-first detection and sampling param.

2025-02-10: Integration harness prototype completed; replayed 5k historical events, initial pass showed 3.6% validation failures concentrated in a single legacy emitter. Created follow-up sub-issue ENG-56109 for emitter-specific rule.
2025-02-12: Canary plan finalized with SLO guardrails (p95 added latency <30ms, validation failure <1%). Scheduling canary for 2025-02-18.
